qt: to the Commission Andi Cristea (S&D) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1457 have significantly reduced tariff quotas for steel imports. Economic operators say that the quota allocated to North Macedonia for category seven steel (heavy quarto plates) is exhausted by the middle of each quarter. For over 12 years, one Romanian shipyard has been buying around 95 % of the plates it needs (6 000-7 000 tonnes/year) from a manufacturer in North Macedonia. Deliveries have now come to a halt even though the order was placed back in January/February 2026. The shipyard has not been able to find an EU-based supplier offering the same surface preparation and deliveries that are synchronised with production. Delays mean shipbuilding for European customers cannot begin on time, entailing potential contractual penalties. 1.
When setting the tariff quota for category seven steel, did the Commission assess the impact on downstream industries, such as shipbuilding, which depend on stable trade flows?
Does the Commission intend to adjust this quota or allow the reallocation of unused volumes when determining the allocations applicable from 2027?
What mechanisms does it have in mind for avoiding disruption of supply to EU users for whom there are no realistic alternatives within the Union?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2026) Regulation (EU) 2026/13841 cuts by 47% the duty-free volumes of steel which can enter the EU market to ensure the survival of the European steelmaking industry. With such reduction of volumes, no supplier can expect to maintain historical volumes of exports of these products to the EU, with the only exception of Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, to which the quota system does not apply. The Commission engaged with North Macedonia in the context of Article XXVIII of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade process and it reached an agreement in principle on the tariff-rate quotas (TRQs) as reflected in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/14572. TRQs for product category seven have been fully exhausted during the first quarter of implementation of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384, with the exception of ‘Free Trade Agreement Quota – Other countries’. Unused TRQs can be carried over to the following quarter within the first year of application of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384. The Commission is monitoring the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384, the TRQs usage and broader effects on the EU market. To this end, a targeted consultation to assess the functioning of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 after its first quarter of implementation was opened between 28 September and 11 October 2026. The Commission is currently assessing the submissions received. The Commission has a continuous empowerment under Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 to adopt Implementing Regulations distributing TRQs. This implies that, should a change linked to one of the applicable criteria under Article 5 occur, the Commission could consider a new TRQs distribution which carefully takes into account all the relevant criteria, in particular the EU interest.
1 Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 June 2026 addressing the

negative trade-related effects of global overcapacity on the Union steel market and amending Regulation (EU) 2020/2170, OJ L, 2026/1384, 24.6.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1384/oj. 2 Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1457 of 29 June 2026 on the distribution of tariff quotas opened under Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 of the European Parliament and of the Council addressing the negative trade-related effects of global overcapacity on the Union steel market and amending Regulation (EU) 2020/2170, OJ L, 2026/1457, 30.6.2026, ELI: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/1457/oj/eng.
